task:
INVESTIGATE ONLY -- DESIGN A GOVERNED PURGE PATH FOR SUPERSEDED RATINGS V4 DERIVED GENERATIONS. This is a read-only planning task: do not modify, create or delete any file, do not push, do not open or comment on a pull request, and do not contact production or any service beyond reading this repository. Base on current origin/main and record its SHA in your answer (expected c774fb09d11a6a5c0f127dc57fa38bbd10216470 or a descendant).

DECISION ALREADY TAKEN BY THE OWNER: docs/ROADMAP.md, in the paragraph beginning "Retaining opt1's roughly 198.5-million system_search rows is currently the only executable path", offers two branches before Finder rollout step 4: accept retention after a measured footprint, or "design and review a governed purge path". The owner has chosen the governed purge path, accepting that docs/operations/infrastructure-status.md (section "V3 database recovery boundary") records that no executable PostgreSQL 18 backup/restore/PITR runbook exists and that recovery is not authorized. Your job is the design a reviewed pull request would implement. Accepting that there is no restore path is not a licence to depend on one: for every destructive step, say what makes it safe without a restore.

READ FIRST, AND CITE file:line FOR EVERY FACTUAL CLAIM: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (authority order, production and Codex boundaries); docs/ROADMAP.md (Finder rollout steps and the purge paragraph); docs/operations/infrastructure-status.md; docs/development/v3-search-spatial-derived-data-decision.md; docs/development/bulk-database-write-safety.md; every file in sql/v3/migrations/ (tables, triggers, guard functions, lifecycle transitions); docs/operations/v3-finder-production-rollout-state.md; scripts/operator/actions/ and .github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml (how governed production operations are run and allowlisted); and the committed production evidence docs/operations/evidence/2026-10-10-v3-derived-lifecycle-status-receipt.json and docs/operations/evidence/2026-10-10-wide-archetype-footprint-200k.json (the receipt's footprint section has the measured database size and free host disk; its derived_generations section has each generation's lifecycle state). Do not take any number or claim in this prompt on trust where the repository can confirm or refute it.

ANSWER WITH THESE NUMBERED SECTIONS. (1) VERIFIED FACTS: which derived generations exist and their lifecycle states; every relation that holds generation-scoped rows; every trigger or guard that constrains deleting, updating or truncating those rows, and exactly under which conditions each permits it; the foreign-key dependencies between those relations; and the measured disk position. Cite each. (2) INVARIANTS the purge must never violate, for example the published generation and everything its reads depend on, anything the schema says must be retained, and the receipt and audit trail. (3) AT LEAST THREE MATERIALLY DIFFERENT APPROACHES, each with: the exact PostgreSQL mechanism used to remove rows and the mechanism that returns space to the filesystem (state explicitly whether a plain DELETE returns space); the lock taken and for how long on tables of this size; the peak additional disk needed at each step against the measured free space; the WAL generated; and the state the database is left in if the step fails or the host dies mid-step. (4) YOUR RECOMMENDED APPROACH in implementable detail: the migration(s), including the guard changes and how everything else stays fail-closed; the operator action(s) and their receipt fields; the allowlist and workflow changes; the order of operations relation by relation, with free disk before and after each step; and the tests and CI lanes that must cover it. (5) WHERE THIS SITS in the Finder rollout steps, and the exact ROADMAP amendment text required -- the ROADMAP outranks every other document, so a design that contradicts it without amending it is not implementable. (6) FAILURE ANALYSIS for each step of your recommendation, given that there is no restore path. (7) WHAT YOU COULD NOT VERIFY, and the questions only the owner can answer.

Be concrete: name files, functions, triggers, columns and states; give arithmetic with units; mark every assumption as an assumption.
